# the contributor audit: discounted repair, actual entropy, and cap-boundary contact

Read the complete stable statements and proofs in:

* `candidate 668d91587751e139`, Sections 1--10;
* `candidate 1fa84e1f531e54da`, Sections 1--10;
* `candidate b5369aed13dad06b`, Sections 1--5.



## 1. The discounted coupling is the principal invariant

For one normal and one endpoint parity, the selected same-marginal coupling satisfies

    b_#(a^d pi) <= omega,
    a=(L(w_-)+L(w_+))/(2L(b)),
    rho=b_#pi=D+E,
    E=b_#((1-a^d)pi).

This is a constraint on the coupling, not merely on its midpoint marginal. It is linear and weakly closed on the compact fixed-marginal class. The roof-cell restriction argument applies to a strongly convex optimizer before any old-law convex-order constraint is imposed. Its output restrictions are disjoint actual output parts; their endpoint supports lie in the closed cells even at ties. The density estimates therefore add without a cell-count factor. The finite-intersection step retains the linear discount while obtaining domination in convex order.

The logarithmic Jensen gap has a fixed-endpoint decomposition. Convex order consequently decreases that gap, although it need not decrease the expectation of the exact discount loss itself. Jensen applied only after this decomposition gives

    E(total) <= m(1-exp(-d Delta_old/m)).

The cube calibration attains equality for a single parity. It is not a sharpness proof for the globally summed 2^n baseline. Normal/parity assembly gives D<=2^n omega; the total error has no additional parity multiplier.

## 2. Affine weights and exact entropy algebra

For positive affine q, the finite global convex extension of F_q=q log(q/L) is justified by the bounded dual-parameter representation. At every pair,

    delta_q/q(b) = log(L(b)/V) + KL(p||s),
    p_i=q(w_i)/(2q(b)),  s_i=L(w_i)/(2V).

Thus delta_q >= -q(b)log a. The weighted mass integral q drho is fixed by the endpoint affine moments, and the same coupling supplies all q-weighted bounds. The q+epsilon passage is uniform on the common compact domain, including the zero-weight case. Replacing q by a hinge would invalidate the affine-moment step and is correctly excluded.

## 3. Actual surface entropy is conditional on a prescribed paired branch

The source-to-midpoint and midpoint-to-average-endpoint Jensen gaps add exactly to the actual surface entropy S. The repair can use Delta_old<=S only when the paired endpoint laws and the source law have the asserted relation. Individual endpoint domination by a useful common projective capacity is an additional hypothesis.

The generic self-pairing has two identical endpoint laws eta. Its diagonal competitor has midpoint eta, dominates any paired midpoint law in convex order, and has zero discount error. Accordingly this construction adds no numerical restriction beyond the original martingale. Nontrivial applications require distinct prescribed endpoint subflows with their actual individual budgets.

For a proper binary subflow, nu=eta-gamma_--gamma_++2rho_b, the exact entropy is S=2Delta_b and the rebuilt error is 2E_b. Both factors are necessary. For the selected separator, R=kappa S with kappa=Delta_sep/((d+1)M_volume); surface-flow mass cannot replace M_volume. The simultaneous power-flattening response has the two negative costs -(R+Delta_sep K_V/(d+1)); no zero or cancellation follows.

## 4. Hinge equality and literal boundary mass

The one-sided stop-loss derivatives are respectively minus closed-cap and minus open-cap mass. At a zero of the nonnegative stop-loss difference, their signs give the two opposite cap inequalities. A boundary-null dominating reference upgrades them to equalities. Attained maximization of a positive finite sum of hinges supplies equality for each hinge after any convex-order improvement within the same feasible class.

For actual normal-preserving surface laws, a fixed cut hyperplane has positive surface mass only at the two parallel normals, except for a null set in the disintegration. At those two normals, its values on the actual graph form a finite set indexed by the integer fibers. Two shifted thresholds within the finite nonzero gap preserve both original open and closed caps, including all original boundary mass. Pure-base cuts use the same finite-gap argument at every normal. The actual inward selector is one of these two conventions; arbitrary fractional trace allocations are not covered.

The relaxed-constraint countable-supremum construction gives a Borel optimal value, and the compact selector then applies to the maximizing class. The original source-compatible class may be imposed in this outer hinge maximization. It is not silently imposed on the internal strong-surplus optimizations used to prove repair.

## 5. Exact remaining obligations

Neither hinge maximization nor entropy repair proves that an actual cap-paying stress coupling lies in the maximizing class or retains its previous cap credit when replaced by a maximizer. The explicit interval example proves that arbitrary prior cap credit can be lost even with no boundary mass. The existence of an actual, distinctly paired, appropriately capped branch with sufficient numerical credit remains unproved. These are therefore verified tools for a possible selected-extremum argument, not a completed selected-extremum argument.
